I think 4 headings in a commit message body of 26 lines is a bit much. Please remove the headings.

Its best to lead with the motivation.

Rather than a "Test Plan", provide unit tests that require the expected behaviour. That way you can remove the entire section.
Thanks for the feedback. I’ve pruned the commit message and included the unit test.
Yes, the log is from obmc-console-client, and the patch resolves my issue. It looks like you’ve proposed a better solution.

Perhaps you can replace the implementation of your patch here with that one 😊

However, maybe something worth considering is updating the logic of `console_socket_path()` to return the derived struct size so that the `addrlen` arithmetic isn't necessary after both calls.
Thanks for the suggestion! I've updated the implementation of console_socket_path() to return the derived struct size. Sorry for the delayed response!

> Thanks for the suggestion! I've updated the implementation of console_socket_path() to return the derived struct size. Sorry for the delayed response!

Reviving this thread: So on closer inspection, my suggestion there set things off down a bad path. PS22 doesn't update the call-site in `set_socket_info()` in `console-server.c`. That call-site expects the returned value to be the length of `sun_path`, not the full struct size. Further, making `console_socket_path()` return the struct size is a bit of hack in terms of its point of abstraction. I think we have have to back out of that.

Hi Sean. I made some comments on the test cases before poking around some more at the uses of `console_socket_path_readable()`. I think there's an issue in console-client.c. Please see the comment on the commit message.
Hi Andrew, thank you for the feedback and for calling out the problems—much appreciated. I guess I should abandon this commit, but if you’d prefer I revise it instead, please let me know.

We only care for abstract socket names. See `console_socket_path()` above.

Why are we adding this case?
Acknowledged

Why have you copied this in? What happens when fixes are applied to the application copy and not here?

There a number of better ways to deal with this:

- Define the meson test to require `console-socket.c` as a source file
- Define the meson test to depend on the object file
- Build the console-server objects into a static library against which you link the test (need to be careful with this though due to the tricks with handler registration).
- `#include "console-socket.c"`
...
Thanks for the suggestion! I've fixed these in the updated unittest script.
This is `memset(3)` but with the parameters swapped.
Acknowledged

Several things here: Can you please avoid the trailing comments to avoid the line-wrap here, and for consistency can you please avoid C++-style comments:


```
/* ensure NUL within sun_path */
strncpy(addr.sun_path, src, sizeof(addr.sun_path));

```


Please fix this throughout.

However, it's not clear what you're trying to suggest with the comment. `sizeof(addr.sun_path)` gives the full length of the destination buffer, and `strncpy()` does not guarantee a NULL terminator if the source string length matches the destination buffer length.


This seems misleading?

Also given the effort you went to with `SOCKET_PATH_MAX` above, why not use that?
Sure. I've also fixed these in the updated unittest script.
`assert(!strcmp(...))`.
Acknowledged
Thanks for reviewing! I've addressed all the feedback in this update.

Ah, so a small wart here:

>       sd_is_socket_unix() is similar to sd_is_socket() but optionally checks
>       the AF_UNIX path the socket is bound to, unless the path parameter is
>       NULL. For normal file system AF_UNIX sockets, set the length parameter
>       to 0. For Linux abstract namespace sockets, set the length to the size
>       of the address, including the initial 0 byte, and set the path to the
>       initial 0 byte of the socket address.

https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man3/sd_is_socket_unix.3.html#DESCRIPTION

This needs to be the length of the content of `addr.sun_path`, not the length of `addr` including the content of `sun_path`. The code will likely cause an out-of-bounds read.

This should be `addrlen - offsetof(struct sockaddr_un, sun_path)`.
What motivated this? No other tests do so. These should be removed throughout.
I think this and the test case above should be combined. I don't see why they should be separated.
@sean.he.wiwynn@gmail.com can you please test PS22?
Hi Andrew, did you mean PS23? I thought you had already updated the code in that patchset. Either way, both PS22 and PS23 work fine on my platform.
Haha, sorry, yes, I did mean PS23. Thanks for testing.
